title: He Last Played a T20I in December 2023. Now Shreyas Iyer Is India's Captain.
excerpt: Iyer replaces World Cup winner Suryakumar Yadav in a leadership reset the selectors called a 'tough decision' made 'in the interest of the team.'
body:
The last time Shreyas Iyer played a T20 International for India, it was December 2023. Hardik Pandya was captain. Suryakumar Yadav had not yet led India to a World Cup title. The Indian Premier League had not yet produced a 15-year-old sensation named Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.

Two and a half years later, Iyer is back — not as a returning middle-order batter trying to reclaim his place, but as India's new T20I captain. The Board of Control for Cricket in India announced the appointment on June 6 as part of the squad selection for the upcoming T20I series against Ireland and England, and later the Asian Games in Japan.

## A Tough Decision

Chief selector Ajit Agarkar acknowledged the difficulty of the call. Suryakumar Yadav had, after all, led India to the T20 World Cup 2026 title on home soil earlier this year. Dropping a World Cup-winning captain is not a move selectors make lightly.

"It's a tough one, having just won the World Cup, but as it happens after most World Cups, you try and reassess what your best way forward is," Agarkar said. "We thought this was the best way forward."

The numbers told a story the selectors could not ignore. In the World Cup itself, Suryakumar scored 242 runs in nine innings at a strike rate of 136.72 — respectable by most standards, but well below his own. In IPL 2026 for Mumbai Indians, he managed just 270 runs in 13 innings at an average of 20.76. At 35, with the next T20 World Cup three years away, the window for a reset was now.

## The Case for Iyer

Shreyas Iyer's credentials as a captain were built in franchise cricket. He led Kolkata Knight Riders to the IPL 2024 title, captained Punjab Kings to a runners-up finish in 2025, and guided them into the playoffs again in 2026. His track record of building teams and extracting performances from young squads is exactly what the selectors wanted.

"Shreyas has been an outstanding captain in the IPL," Agarkar noted. "His reputation as a good leader helped him clinch the job." At 31, Iyer is young enough to see through a full cycle of T20I assignments but experienced enough to handle the weight of captaining India.

The ODI squad for the Afghanistan series reinforced the signal: Iyer was named vice-captain under Shubman Gill, formalising a leadership structure that places him at the centre of India's white-ball future.

## The New Guard

Alongside Iyer, the selectors announced Tilak Varma as vice-captain — a 23-year-old left-hander from Hyderabad who has played 49 T20Is and scored nearly 1,400 runs at an average of 44. Varma replaces Axar Patel in the deputy's role and brings a generational shift to the leadership group.

The squad itself signals intent. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, the IPL 2026 Orange Cap winner with 776 runs at a strike rate of 237.30, received his maiden India call-up. Lucknow Super Giants pacer Prince Yadav — who dismissed Virat Kohli with a peach of a delivery during the IPL — earned selections for both the ODI and T20I squads after taking 16 wickets in 14 matches.

Ishan Kishan returns to the setup after nearly three years away, his domestic form and IPL performances finally earning him a second chance.

## What Changes

For NRIs who followed India's T20 World Cup triumph with pride, the leadership change may feel abrupt. But the BCCI's logic is consistent with its post-World Cup pattern. After the 2007 T20 World Cup, India moved on from Dhoni's T20I captaincy within two years. After the 2024 title, Rohit Sharma stepped back from T20Is. Now Suryakumar follows.

Iyer's challenge is different from his predecessors'. He inherits a squad in transition, with senior stalwarts like Rohit, Kohli, and Bumrah rested or absent from the T20I setup. The Ireland and England tours — five T20Is across Belfast, Dublin, and English venues — will be his first test. The Asian Games in Nagoya, where cricket makes its return to the multi-sport event, will be his showcase.

Suryakumar, for his part, responded with quiet grace. Within hours of the announcement, he posted on social media backing the team and congratulating Sooryavanshi on his maiden call-up. No bitterness, no public frustration — just the dignity of a man who knows he won India something they will never forget.

The captaincy has changed hands. The ambition remains the same.
